items.text: The Day of Rebirth

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: This is ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I see.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I remember it now. I've seen it before.
At that moment, when I took the mirror from Elbert's hand, I was almost burned by the heat of the handle.
I imagined him tightly gripping the mirror with the only hand he had left as he awkwardly stood at the door of my clinic.
That was not an image I wanted to see.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Look at this thing! I can see the glue between the cracks, and these pieces don't even go together. You're really bad at this, aren't you?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It looks like you've never once worked with your hands, er, hand.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Klara!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Why didn't you just take it to the factory and ask them to do the work? They're professionals. At least they could've coated the mirror with silver to cover the cracks.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: In its current state, my reflection is split and shattered, too. It's almost incomprehensible.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: But ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Pull yourself together and stop fidgeting! Be a gentleman, Elbert!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And I will be a lady and keep my promise. Not to apologize, but to reflect myself.
I wasn't only talking to Elbert, but also to myself. It was an announcement.
I took a deep breath and tried to recall the feeling of casting my arcane skill.
But the mirror reflected nothing.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Hmm, I don't see anything.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: That's odd.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Or does this mean I have no desires? Interesting. Heinrich would like to know about this.
She studies her reflection between the cracks in the mirror.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But it doesn't feel right. Perhaps because it was broken?

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Be patient, Klara.
Before he could finish his sentence, the image in the mirror twisted, revealing an object within it.
Though the cracks split it into many pieces, I could still recognize it.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What is this? A new mirror?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What do you mean?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Is this my innermost desire?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I, I saw it before.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: In the hand mirror Elbert fixed for me.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I saw another hand mirror reflected in the shattered one.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I thought my arcane skill didn't work, but upon reflection, maybe it did work. This must be the symbol of my dream, my desire.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Back then, I wanted a new mirror.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: An independent, free kingdom. A new world for arcanists.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Hah. A brand new world. I wanted it, and I got it.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But this was never my intention.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I've always tried to do something—to make a change. But what can I do if I can't even undo the hypnosis on my own patient?
She closes her eyes bitterly. When she opens them, her eyes are fixed on the shard in her hand yet again.
Moments before, when she cast her arcane skill, a mirror appeared in it.
The mirror covered in cracks and glue marks.
The mirror Zemfira gave her.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Is this because I can't seem to shake the thought of this hand mirror, or is it another illusion of my arcane skill?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: My innermost desire, revealed by my arcane skill, is still the mirror given to me by Zemfira?
With Zemfira's name in her heart, she decides to try it again.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Zemfira, you once prayed for my safety.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: So could you tell me if it's real? I shouldn't hurt myself to confirm its existence, should I?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It's been an illusion so many times. It has to be real just this once, doesn't it?
She rubs the shard, trying to erase the image reflected within it.
No matter how hard she tries, the reflection remains firm.
She casts her arcane skill again, but nothing changes. The hand mirror, given by her friend, broken by herself, and put back together by her brother, still sits in its reflection.
Despite its repair, its cracks are still clearly visible. Like in life, no matter how much you heal, the damage will always be there.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The cracked mirror ... How did I not see it?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The marks here show it must've been shattered before.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I know it's not perfect.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It's not even a very useful mirror.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But still ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I wish so dearly for it to be in my hands.
A teardrop falls silently on the shard.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I know that civilization is fragile, that life is fragile.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But if life is destined to be broken, if society is doomed to be shattered,

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: then we should at least try to repair it.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Because we can't—we shouldn't—live in a broken society!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: This has always been my dream, from the very beginning.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I just want everyone to find their happiness, to lead a harmonious life together.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Why didn't I realize it sooner?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Why didn't I tell Isolde, Elbert, and Zemfira? Why didn't I tell them earlier?!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Why did I say those pompous, flowery things to Isolde instead of the simple truth?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Why was I so cruel to Elbert when I could have expressed my joy and gratitude to have him as a brother?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And, Zemfira. I was too young and naive to give her my encouragement—to express my wishes for her.
Teardrops rain down on the shard, running on its surface,
and gathering in the cracks of the hand mirror within.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Why couldn't I fix Vienna?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: In the way Elbert fixed this mirror for me?
She's managed to regain her arcane skill, but it's not enough to fill the hollow in her heart.
Her friend can no longer hear her confession. The only thing left is this reflection of her gift.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The prophecy of Zemfira. So then this mirror will not bring us disaster, rather, it has already protected us from one.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: She gave me this blessing, yet I lost her mirror. I lost the whole of Vienna.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: If only they could be here with me.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: If only I could touch this mirror again.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: If only ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I could fix everything.
A knock on the door pulls her back to reality.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member I
items.text: Ms. Kakania!

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member I
items.text: We've been informed that you applied for an arcane skill experiment. We're here to take you to the field.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member I
items.text: Are you ready?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Oh, I completely forgot.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I've been spending so much time blaming myself that I ignored the most important thing.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The thing that can be done by me, and only me:

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: To bring together the broken pieces, to fix the mistake I made.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: To undo the hypnosis on Isolde.
She holds up the shard and looks at it through the light from the window. There's nothing in it anymore.
But Kakania knows there was a hand mirror in it, vivid and clear.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Thank you, Zemfira. Thank you, Elbert.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member I
items.text: Ms. Kakania? Are you there?
The staff member opens the door and is startled to see Kakania already standing in the room.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Yes! Thank you for coming.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'm almost ready!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Is there anything else I need to do?

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member I
items.text: Yes, here are the things to note:

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member I
items.text: First, please remove any items that might damage yourself or the experimentation field, such as jewelry.
